newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: White House optimistic about APEC infotech stand.
newsitem.headline: White House optimistic about APEC infotech stand.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton expects Asia-Pacific leaders to strongly endorse his drive to conclude a global agreement on free trade in computers and telecommunications equipment, a U.S. spokesman said on Monday.

"The president has been working that issue himself... when the (APEC) declaration is read later today we'll see if they put a little more oomph into this issue than the APEC ministers did," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Trade and foreign ministers at the annual summit agreed last week to back the U.S.-led effort to conclude an information technology agreement by next month's inaugural meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore.

But it was far from the ringing endorsement that Washington had wanted. While McCurry stopped short of saying the final declaration of the APEC conference would set a specific date for the elimination of tariffs on infotech products, he suggested that Clinton would be pleased with the end result.
"His number one goal here in Manila was to press hard on measures that would free up trade in information technology," McCurry said.

Clinton informally lobbied other participants in the summit of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum on the issue at a private dinner on Sunday night. The summit began on Monday at a former U.S. naval base at Subic Bay, north of Manila.
